env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local
mkdir $WORK/bin

# Imported closed unions: member identity across the package boundary.
# A LoGOs importer accepts only the concrete members the owner
# declares. The member set includes an owner-private concrete member
# that importers can obtain only through an exported factory and
# cannot name, and instantiated generic member types with the same
# underlying shape but distinct type arguments, which are distinct
# members: a same-shape instantiation with a third type argument is
# rejected. A method-compatible non-member is rejected in LoGOs
# source. The Go-facing projection of an exported value union is
# methods-only by design, so a Go client may still pass a non-member
# that implements the method set; that hole is asserted here on
# purpose and lives only in the Go module. A union with a nil-capable
# member carries a present typed-nil payload: the union value is
# non-nil, the switch matches the pointer member, and the option form
# keeps presence separate from payload nil.
#
# The good module (w/own) and the two negative modules (negm, negs)
# are separate modules so a bad fixture never blocks the good
# ejection. Rejection is checked at the compile boundary of the
# native build only: the ejected form is a methods-only interface,
# which Go cannot distinguish members from method-compatible
# non-members, so parity is asserted on the good module's run output.

cd w/own
logos build ./...
logos build -o $WORK/bin/own$GOEXE .
exec $WORK/bin/own$GOEXE
stdout '^word:hi$'
stdout '^tag:n$'
stdout '^kind word tag$'
stdout '^arm default: word:hi$'
stdout '^present typed-nil: true word$'
stdout '^none absent: true$'
stdout '^boxed present: true$'
stdout '^boxed kind word$'
stdout '^slot int member: true false$'
stdout '^slot string member: true false$'
stdout '^slot label slot$'
cp stdout $WORK/native.txt
cd ../..

cd w/goq
logos build -o $WORK/bin/goq$GOEXE .
exec $WORK/bin/goq$GOEXE
stdout '^N$'
stdout '^word:go$'
cd ../..

# Imported union rejects a concrete non-member that implements the
# method set.
cd negm
! logos build ./...
stderr 'cannot use'
cd ..

# Imported union rejects a same-shape instantiation whose type
# argument is not in the member set.
cd negs
! logos build ./...
stderr 'cannot use'
cd ..

# The good module ejects and the ejected output builds and runs with
# the upstream toolchain, byte-identical to the native run.
cd w/own
logos eject -o $WORK/out
cd $WORK/out
exists $UPROOT1272/bin/go
exec env -u GOROOT $UPROOT1272/bin/go build ./...
exec env -u GOROOT $UPROOT1272/bin/go run .
cmp stdout $WORK/native.txt

-- w/own/go.mod --
module example.com/own

go 1.27

-- w/own/own/own.lgo --
package own

// word is the owner-private concrete member of Token. Importers
// obtain word values only through the exported factories below and
// cannot name the type, so the exhaustive switch over every member
// runs here.
type word struct {
	s string
}

func (w word) Label() string {
	return "word:" + w.s
}

// Tag is the exported member of Token.
type Tag struct {
	Name string
}

func (t Tag) Label() string {
	return "tag:" + t.Name
}

// Token is a closed value union exported to importers. *word is a
// nil-capable member, so Token? carries explicit presence: a present
// typed-nil payload stays distinct from none.
type Token interface {
	*word | Tag
	Label() string
}

// Word returns the private member through an exported factory.
func Word(s string) Token {
	w := word{s: s}
	return &w
}

// Box carries a Token field across the boundary. The typed nil is
// stored by field assignment; returning the typed nil itself as a
// union result is the compile error correctness::typed_nil_return.
type Box struct {
	T Token
}

// FillNil stores the private member as a typed nil payload in the
// field, the form the JSON wire fixtures prove. The union value in
// the field is present; its payload is a nil *word.
func FillNil(b *Box) {
	b.T = (*word)(nil)
}

// Kind switches over every member and nil. Only the owner can name
// all of them.
func Kind(t Token) string {
	switch t.(type) {
	case *word:
		return "word"
	case Tag:
		return "tag"
	case nil:
		return "nil"
	}
	return "unreachable"
}

func Who(t Token) string {
	return t.Label()
}

// Slot is one generic type; the members below are two pointer
// instantiations of it with distinct type arguments and the same
// underlying shape.
type Slot[T any] struct {
	V T
}

func (s Slot[T]) Label() string {
	return "slot"
}

// SlotPair is a closed union over *Slot[int] and *Slot[string]. They
// are distinct members: *Slot[float64] is a non-member.
type SlotPair interface {
	*Slot[int] | *Slot[string]
	Label() string
}

func NumSlot(n int) SlotPair {
	return &Slot[int]{V: n}
}

func TextSlot(s string) SlotPair {
	return &Slot[string]{V: s}
}

-- w/own/main.lgo --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/own/own"
)

func main() {
	w := own.Word("hi")
	fmt.Println(own.Who(w))
	fmt.Println(own.Who(own.Tag{Name: "n"}))
	fmt.Println("kind", own.Kind(w), own.Kind(own.Tag{Name: "n"}))

	switch v := w.(type) {
	case own.Tag:
		fmt.Println("arm tag:", v.Name)
	case nil:
		fmt.Println("arm nil")
	default:
		fmt.Println("arm default:", w.Label())
	}

	var nb own.Box
	own.FillNil(&nb)
	nilw := nb.T
	fmt.Println("present typed-nil:", nilw != nil, own.Kind(nilw))

	var none own.Token?
	fmt.Println("none absent:", none == nil)

	var boxed own.Token? = nilw
	fmt.Println("boxed present:", boxed != nil)
	if boxed != nil {
		fmt.Println("boxed kind", own.Kind(boxed))
	}

	n := own.NumSlot(5)
	s := own.TextSlot("s")
	_, okInt := n.(*own.Slot[int])
	_, okWrongArg := n.(*own.Slot[string])
	fmt.Println("slot int member:", okInt, okWrongArg)
	_, okStr := s.(*own.Slot[string])
	_, okWrongArg2 := s.(*own.Slot[int])
	fmt.Println("slot string member:", okStr, okWrongArg2)
	fmt.Println("slot label", n.Label())
}

-- w/goq/go.mod --
module example.com/goq

go 1.27

require example.com/own v0.0.0

replace example.com/own => ../own

-- w/goq/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/own/own"
)

// N implements the method set of own.Token without being a member.
// The Go-facing projection of an exported value union is methods-only
// by design, so this call compiles and runs; the LoGOs importer of
// the same union rejects the same assignment (see negm).
type N struct{}

func (n N) Label() string { return "N" }

func main() {
	fmt.Println(own.Who(N{}))
	fmt.Println(own.Who(own.Word("go")))
}

-- negm/go.mod --
module example.com/negm

go 1.27

require example.com/own v0.0.0

replace example.com/own => ../w/own

-- negm/negm.lgo --
package negm

import (
	"example.com/own/own"
)

// C implements the method set of own.Token but is not a member. A
// LoGOs importer must reject the assignment at compile time.
type C struct {
	Z int
}

func (c C) Label() string {
	return "C"
}

var _ own.Token = C{Z: 1}

-- negs/go.mod --
module example.com/negs

go 1.27

require example.com/own v0.0.0

replace example.com/own => ../w/own

-- negs/negs.lgo --
package negs

import (
	"example.com/own/own"
)

// *Slot[float64] has the same underlying shape as the members of
// own.SlotPair but a distinct type argument, so it is not a member.
// A LoGOs importer must reject the assignment at compile time.
var _ own.SlotPair = &own.Slot[float64]{V: 1.5}
